name: Clenbuterol
lead: Clenbuterol is a long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist developed as a bronchodilator for asthma and other airway obstruction, and widely used in veterinary medicine, mainly for horses. People who use it for their looks take it as an oral fat-loss and muscle-retention aid while dieting: the aim is a leaner, more defined physique, with visible abs, a tighter waist and more vascularity, achieved by lowering body fat while holding on to muscle. It is approved as a human medicine in some countries but not in the United States [1][2][34].

The idea of using it for body composition goes back to animal research in the 1980s, which reported shifts toward muscle and away from fat in rodents and livestock [16][17], and to the bodybuilding scene of the late 1980s, where the author Dan Duchaine is credited with introducing it to bodybuilders [35][34]. A 1995 review described its popularity among athletes as a substitute for anabolic steroids [2]. Anti-doping bodies list it as a prohibited anabolic agent [2][34].

Human research on the looks-related claims is sparse. A 2025 randomized trial in 11 healthy men reported higher lean mass and muscle protein accretion after short clenbuterol cycles, along with reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and blunted muscle beta-2 signalling [6]. Case reports and a 2023 systematic review in athletes describe heart rhythm disturbances, myocarditis, infarction and death [4][11]. On looksmax.org and T Nation it is discussed as a cheap fat-loss pill, often compared with GLP-1 drugs, cardarine and DNP [27][28][29][32][33].

paras: Bodybuilders and physique competitors use clenbuterol during "cutting" phases, when the goal is to strip fat while keeping muscle [2][34]. Reviews of weight-loss products list it among agents sold online [5]. Users on looksmax.org describe it as a way to reach visible abs or a leaner face and body, often alongside lifting and a calorie deficit, and compare it with GLP-1 drugs, cardarine, DNP and growth hormone [27][28][29][32].

Practitioners usually describe it as one part of a stack rather than a stand-alone method, and discuss on-off patterns because the body's response to beta-2 stimulation fades over time; the 2025 trial found that muscle beta-2 signalling was desensitized after the drug cycles [6]. This article does not give doses or schedules.

Clenbuterol was introduced as an asthma bronchodilator, with approvals in Germany reported from 1977 and in other countries including Mexico [1][34]. A 2024 trial compared an ambroxol and clenbuterol oral solution with a Chinese medicine product in 480 children with acute bronchitis [7]. In large-animal practice it is used as a uterine relaxant during difficult births, and in horses as an aerosol for allergic airway disease [8][34]. Researchers have also tested it in chronic heart failure, where lean mass rose without an endurance improvement, and registered trials cover ALS, Pompe disease, spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy and FSHD [10][19][22][23][18][36].

Clenbuterol selectively stimulates beta-2 adrenoceptors, relaxing bronchial smooth muscle through cyclic AMP, with a longer duration of action than salbutamol or isoprenaline in guinea pig tissue [1][3][14]. Wikipedia describes it as structurally and pharmacologically similar to epinephrine and salbutamol, but more potent and longer acting, with high oral absorption, minimal liver metabolism and an elimination half-life of roughly 36 to 48 hours [34].

Its effects on muscle and fat are attributed to beta-2 signalling in those tissues: in rats, chronic beta-2 agonist treatment altered body composition and protein turnover [16], though a 1986 study of clenbuterol-stimulated muscle growth found no effect on muscle protein biosynthesis, suggesting the growth came from reduced protein breakdown or other mechanisms [17]. Wikipedia notes that the ergogenic effects resemble those of stimulants such as ephedrine more than those of anabolic steroids [34].

The 2025 Journal of Physiology randomized controlled trial gave healthy men oral clenbuterol or placebo in two 2-week cycles separated by a 3-week washout, and reported increased lean mass and muscle protein accretion, reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and blunted muscle beta-2 adrenergic signalling; its authors describe the drug as previously unexplored in randomized trials for these purposes [6].

A heart-failure trial reported more lean muscle mass but no endurance benefit [10], and a combined drug and ventricular assist device protocol that included clenbuterol studied myocardial recovery [12][13][20]. Registered studies include a trial on muscle memory with resistance training, studies of beta-2 stimulation and muscle glucose uptake including in people with obesity, and a study of responses in healthy humans [21][24][25][26]. A cognition study compared three beta-adrenoceptor drugs in healthy volunteers and Parkinson's disease [9]. No trial has measured fat loss or appearance in healthy dieters.

A 2023 systematic review of 23 reports covering 24 athletes found supraventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, hypotension, chest pain, myocardial injury, myocarditis, ischemia, infarction, cardiomyopathy, hepatomegaly, hyperglycemia and death, with cardiac complications most common and oral ingestion the usual route [4]. Individual case reports describe clenbuterol-induced myocarditis [11].

Wikipedia lists nervousness, tremor, tachycardia, raised blood pressure and thyrotoxicosis-like effects, and notes reports of nausea, vomiting, sweating and palpitations among people using it for weight loss or athletic performance [34]. In 2021 the Mexican fitness influencer Odalis Santos Mena died of cardiac arrest during a cosmetic procedure under anesthesia; a coroner attributed the death to a combination of clenbuterol and the anesthetic, according to Wikipedia [34]. Contaminated or mislabeled supplements have been documented in doping analyses [15].
Clenbuterol was patented in 1967 and entered medical use in 1977 [34]. Grokipedia credits Boehringer Ingelheim with synthesizing it and reports a US veterinary approval in 1998 [1].

Interest in its effect on body composition came from livestock and rodent research in the 1980s [16][17]. Dan Duchaine, a bodybuilding author whose Underground Steroid Handbook series began in 1981, is credited with introducing it to bodybuilders in 1988; Wikipedia says the anabolic claim likely originated in equine research and spread through bodybuilding [35][34]. A 1995 review in Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise asked whether it was a substitute for anabolic steroids and noted a US Olympic Committee ban [2].
Its image outside bodybuilding grew through celebrity gossip and, later, online fitness and looksmaxxing forums, where it sits among the cheaper oral options for cutting [34][28].

Because clenbuterol was used illegally as a growth promoter in cattle and pigs, residues in meat have caused mass poisonings. Wikipedia reports suspected veal liver poisoning in France (22 people) and Spain (135 people) in 1990; about 50 cases in Portugal between 1998 and 2002; roughly 330 people in Shanghai in September 2006; at least 70 in Guangdong in 2009; and a 2011 Henan case involving a subsidiary of Shuanghui Group that led to 72 detentions, followed by a Chinese ban in September 2011 [34]. The US banned it in meat animals in 1991 and the EU in 1996 [34][1].

Contamination complicates anti-doping: authorities must distinguish deliberate use from accidental ingestion, and use can be confirmed in urine or semen [34]. WADA lists the drug as an anabolic agent, which Wikipedia says was done without evidence of an anabolic effect in humans [34].

Wikipedia reports it is prescription-only in the UK and Australia (Schedule 4) and that the FDA bans its use in any animal that could enter the human food chain; it is not part of any FDA-approved human therapy [34]. It is prohibited for athletes subject to IOC testing [34][2]. Sellers online often label it as a research or veterinary product.

Forum threads on looksmax.org include questions from teenagers about using it to get abs, discussions of ordering from online pharmacies, and arguments about whether before-and-after transformations that combine clen with DNP are worth the risk [27][28][30]. A 2020 T Nation post describes it as keeping the poster alert on night shifts [33]. Press coverage has linked it to celebrities seeking weight loss, and to fitness-influencer deaths such as the 2021 Santos Mena case [34].

Related compounds discussed in the same circles include albuterol (salbutamol), ephedrine and caffeine stacks, cimaterol and mabuterol, and non-stimulant fat-loss agents such as cardarine and GLP-1 drugs [34][29][32].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, clenbuterol is treated as an inexpensive oral fat-loss drug, often named alongside cardarine, DNP, HGH and GLP-1 compounds [27][28][29][32].

claims.claim: Clen is a cheap way to get shredded
claims.believers: A user reports seeing good progress in others and notes the low price per tablet and a dislike of GLP-1 agonists [28]. Another thread asks about starting it for abs after a year of lifting [27].
claims.experts: A randomized trial in healthy men found increased lean mass but reduced fitness, and the athlete case literature documents cardiac harms; no trial tests it for fat loss in healthy people [6][4].

claims.claim: Clen is stronger than GW (cardarine) but has worse side effects
claims.believers: A poster in a clen versus cardarine thread says clen sides are worse but that clen is stronger [29].
claims.experts: No published comparison exists; reports describe cardiac adverse events with clenbuterol [4].

claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread asks whether clenbuterol causes more vascularity [31].
claims.experts: No published studies were found on vascularity; documented effects include tachycardia and hypotension [4].

claims.claim: Clen plus DNP and other drugs produce dramatic transformations
claims.believers: Users discuss running clen with HGH, cardarine and DNP and debate transformation results [30][32].
claims.experts: A review of weight-loss toxicity covers DNP and other agents sold online, and case reports document serious adverse events with clenbuterol [5][4].

claims.claim: Clen preserves or builds muscle while cutting
claims.believers: Bodybuilders say it keeps them full and hard while dieting; the claim traces to the 1980s livestock and rodent work and to Duchaine's circle [35][16].
claims.experts: A 2025 randomized trial found more lean mass in healthy men but worse fitness and desensitized receptors; a 1986 rat study found no change in muscle protein synthesis [6][17]. The anabolic label in doping lists is described by Wikipedia as lacking human evidence [34].

claims.claim: It must be cycled because the body stops responding
claims.believers: Users describe on-off patterns to keep the effect from fading [28].
claims.experts: The 2025 trial reported blunted muscle beta-2 signalling after two short cycles, consistent with desensitization [6].

claims.claim: A positive test can be blamed on contaminated meat
claims.believers: Athletes who tested positive have argued that they ate contaminated food.
claims.experts: Contaminated meat has caused mass poisonings in Spain, France, China and elsewhere, which is why anti-doping authorities must weigh intent [34].

claims.claim: Clen works as a stimulant for alertness and energy
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says it keeps them alert on night shifts [33].
claims.experts: Wikipedia compares its performance effects to ephedrine or amphetamine and lists tachycardia, tremor and nervousness among effects [34].

card.summary: Asthma-drug stimulant used as a gray-market cutting pill, with a documented record of heart problems.
card.note: Not approved for humans in the US; case reports of arrhythmia, myocarditis and death; banned in sport.

quick.overview:
Clenbuterol is a beta-2 agonist made as an asthma bronchodilator. It is not approved for people in the US but is bought online by bodybuilders and others for fat loss.

The only randomized trial in healthy men reported added lean mass but poorer cardiorespiratory fitness.
quick.mechanism: It activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, which relax airways and, in muscle and fat tissue, are linked to protein accretion and fat breakdown. Receptors can become less responsive with repeated use.
quick.risks: Case reports in athletes describe fast heartbeat, atrial fibrillation, chest pain, myocarditis, heart attack and death. It is banned in sport and in food animals, and unregulated supply can be mislabeled or contaminated.

angle.text: People take clenbuterol during a diet to get leaner, hoping to show more muscle definition and a sharper jaw and waist as body fat drops. The animal and human data show higher lean mass in some settings, and users add it to calorie deficits rather than using it alone.
